# Strata { .landing-title }

**Strata is a notebook your coding agent can drive, and everything it computes stays.**

![A terminal running strata CLI commands beside a browser on the same notebook, over seven moments: the empty notebook, a load cell arriving, the cell running, finishing after about two seconds, a summarize cell arriving that reads its variable, both cells green, and the load cell run again and served from the cache in milliseconds.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/web-agent-live-light.gif#only-light){ .hero }
![A terminal running strata CLI commands beside a browser on the same notebook, over seven moments: the empty notebook, a load cell arriving, the cell running, finishing after about two seconds, a summarize cell arriving that reads its variable, both cells green, and the load cell run again and served from the cache in milliseconds.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/web-agent-live-dark.gif#only-dark){ .hero }

*An agent adds and runs cells through the `strata` CLI while the browser on the same
session updates. Captured from a real run, not a mock-up.*

<div class="grid cards" markdown>

-   **Coding agent**

    ---

    Hand a notebook to Claude Code and watch it build through MCP tools.

    [Use a coding agent →](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/agent/)

-   **Web UI**

    ---

    Write and run cells yourself, with rendered tables, plots and the DAG.

    [Your first notebook →](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/notebook/)

-   **Terminal**

    ---

    Watch a notebook live from a second pane or an SSH session. Read-only.

    [Terminal viewer →](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/tui/)

</div>

## Install

=== "uv (recommended)"

    ```bash
    uv tool install "strata-notebook[mcp,tui]"
    strata-notebook
    ```

    Then open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765). The `mcp`
    and `tui` extras are what `strata agent` and `strata watch` need.
    Plain `pip install` is not supported.

=== "Docker"

    ```bash
    docker compose up -d --build
    ```

    Then open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765).

    Or run the prebuilt image (linux/amd64), published with each release:

    ```bash
    docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8765:8765 -v strata_state:/home/strata/.strata \
      ghcr.io/bearing-research/strata:0.11.0
    ```

=== "From source"

    ```bash
    uv sync
    cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
    uv run strata-notebook
    ```

    Then open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765).

See [Install](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/installation/) for full details.

## Why the work holds up

**[Nothing runs twice.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/caching/)** A cell's identity is its source, its
inputs and its environment. The step an agent ran ten turns ago is a cache hit now, and
an edit re-runs only the cells below it.

![A browser on the tutorial notebook over five moments: nothing has run; Run All computes every cell; Run All again and every code cell is a cache hit showing the time it saved; one cell is edited, so it and the chart below read stale while the load cell stays cached; Run All again, and only those two run while the load cell still reads cached, saved 2.1s.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/cache-payoff-light.gif#only-light)
![A browser on the tutorial notebook over five moments: nothing has run; Run All computes every cell; Run All again and every code cell is a cache hit showing the time it saved; one cell is edited, so it and the chart below read stale while the load cell stays cached; Run All again, and only those two run while the load cell still reads cached, saved 2.1s.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/cache-payoff-dark.gif#only-dark)

*Edit one cell in `strata tutorial`: only the cells that read it run again, and the
cell above keeps what it saved. Captured from a real run, not a mock-up.*

**[No wiring to maintain.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/dag-and-staleness/)** Strata reads each cell to
find what it uses and what it defines, and shows which results an edit has left stale.

**[Every result knows where it came from.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/artifacts-and-lineage/)** Every
output is a versioned artifact, so you can trace it back through what produced it.

**[It reads like code in git.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/file-format-and-git/)** A notebook is one
plain-text file per cell plus a TOML manifest. Outputs and caches stay in a gitignored folder.

There is more on the [Features](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/features/) page, and Strata also works
[as a library](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/core/).

Strata is pre-1.0, so the API may change between 0.x minors; pin to a minor if you need
stability.

<!-- https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/installation/index.md -->

# Install

## Prerequisites

- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) ≥ 0.8** - install via the
  [uv installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)
  (`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` on macOS/Linux;
  PowerShell installer on Windows). uv fetches a compatible Python
  automatically, so you don't need Python 3.12+ pre-installed. Strata
  refuses to start outside a uv-managed env.
- **[Node.js 26+](https://nodejs.org/)** - only if building the
  frontend from source.

Windows: source builds work via WSL2 (smoother) or native Windows
(uv and Node have Windows installers). Day-to-day dev is on
macOS/Linux; WSL2 is the better-trodden path.

## From PyPI (recommended)

```bash
uv tool install strata-notebook
strata-notebook
```

This puts `strata-notebook`, `strata`, `strata-notebook-tui` and
`strata-worker` on `PATH` in a uv-managed tool environment. The wheel
is pure Python and ships the frontend prebuilt. Plain `pip install`
is not supported; see the uv requirement above.

Add extras in brackets, for example
`uv tool install "strata-notebook[mcp,tui]"` for `strata agent`:

| Extra | Enables |
| --- | --- |
| `mcp` | The `/mcp` endpoint a coding agent connects to. `strata agent` needs it. |
| `tui` | The terminal viewer: `strata watch`, `strata-notebook-tui`, and `strata agent` unless you pass `--no-tui`. |
| `sql` | SQL cells. Add a driver extra for each database you connect to: `sql-duckdb`, `sql-sqlite`, `sql-postgres`, `sql-snowflake`, `sql-bigquery`. |
| `postgres` | A Postgres metadata database for the artifact store (`STRATA_ARTIFACT_METADATA_DSN`), for several nodes sharing one store. |
| `azure` | The Azure Blob Storage artifact backend, notebook `az://` mounts, and reading Azure lake tables (`adlfs`). |
| `s3` | The S3 artifact backend (`STRATA_ARTIFACT_BLOB_BACKEND=s3`, through boto3, presigned build-manifest URLs included) and notebook `s3://` mounts (`s3fs`). |
| `gcs` | The GCS artifact backend (`STRATA_ARTIFACT_BLOB_BACKEND=gcs`, through google-cloud-storage, presigned build-manifest URLs included) and notebook `gs://` mounts (`gcsfs`). |
| `otel` | OpenTelemetry tracing. |
| `notebook` | The cell runtime libraries (pandas, numpy, orjson, cloudpickle, matplotlib, Pillow) in Strata's own environment. A remote worker image needs it; a local server does not, since each notebook gets its own venv. |

## GitHub Codespaces (zero setup)

Click **"Open in Codespaces"** on the [repo](https://github.com/bearing-research/strata)
and the server is running by the time the browser tab opens. No local
toolchain needed. See [Codespaces](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/deployment/codespaces/) for what
the devcontainer provisions.

## Docker (easiest)

No local toolchain required:

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

Open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765) in your browser.

Releases after 0.9.0 also publish the image as `ghcr.io/bearing-research/strata:<version>`;
see [Docker → Prebuilt image](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/deployment/docker/#prebuilt-image).

## From source

### 1. Install dependencies

```bash
uv sync
```

This installs all Python dependencies and Strata itself, editable.

### 2. Build the frontend (optional)

If you want the notebook UI served by the backend:

```bash
cd frontend
npm ci
npm run build
cd ..
```

The server serves `src/strata/_frontend/` if it exists, else
`frontend/dist/`. `_frontend/` is the bundle a release copies in, so after a
fresh build either copy `frontend/dist/` into `src/strata/_frontend/` or
remove `src/strata/_frontend/`.

### 3. Start the server

```bash
uv run strata-notebook
```

Or equivalently:

```bash
uv run python -m strata
```

The server starts on port 8765 by default. Open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765).

## Verify

```bash
curl http://localhost:8765/health
# {"status":"ok"}
```

## Commands reference

The PyPI package is `strata-notebook`; the installed Python module
and CLI binary are both named `strata`.

The table assumes a source checkout, where `uv run` resolves each command
inside the project venv. After `uv tool install`, drop the `uv run` prefix
and call `strata-notebook` / `strata` / `strata-worker` directly.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `uv run strata-notebook` | Start the HTTP server (notebook UI + REST API). Same as `uv run python -m strata`. |
| `uv run strata run <notebook-dir>` | Headless notebook execution for CI / scheduled runs. See [CLI](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/cli/). |
| `uv run strata validate <notebook-dir>` | Static checks (schema, annotations, DAG) without executing. See [CLI](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/cli/#strata-validate). |
| `uv run strata tutorial [name]` | Copy a bundled sample into the notebook storage directory under a fresh name, open it and print its URL, starting a server if none is running. With no name, list the samples. See [Quickstart](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/notebook/#1-take-the-tutorial). |
| `uv run strata new <name>` | Scaffold a notebook directory. See [CLI](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/cli/#strata-new). |
| `uv run strata cell <action>`, `strata dag`, `strata status`, `strata dep <action>` | Agent-facing notebook tooling: inspect (`cell list/show`, `dag`, `status`), save a display output such as a plot to a file (`cell output`), execute (`cell run/test`), cancel a server run (`cell cancel`, `--server/--session` only), and author (`cell add/edit/rm/mv/annotate`, `cell pin-fetch`, `dep add/rm`) - offline against a directory or `--server/--session` against a running server. See [Notebook CLI](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/cli/#inspecting-a-notebook-cell-dag-status). |
| `uv run strata worker <action>` | Manage a notebook's workers: `ls`, `add`/`rm`/`default` (local, edits `notebook.toml`), and `add-ssh`/`rm-ssh` (provision + tunnel a worker over SSH, against a running server). See [Workers](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/workers/#run-cells-on-a-machine-you-can-ssh-to). |
| `uv run strata agent <notebook-dir>` | One-command on-ramp for driving a notebook with a coding agent: create-or-open the notebook, start (or reuse) a server with the MCP endpoint enabled, open a session, write the `.mcp.json` + `CLAUDE.md` the agent needs, and attach the TUI (skip it with `--no-tui` and watch in the web UI instead). Then run `claude` in the notebook directory to drive it live. Needs the `[mcp]` extra, plus `[tui]` unless you pass `--no-tui`. See [Use a coding agent](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/agent/). |
| `uv run strata export <notebook-dir>` | Render a notebook to markdown or HTML (add `--app-view` for a frozen dashboard snapshot), or write a portable snapshot zip with `--to snapshot`. See [Export and import](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/export/). |
| `uv run strata import <file>` | Convert a Jupyter `.ipynb` into a Strata notebook directory, or unpack a snapshot zip back into one. See [Coming from Jupyter](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/import/). |
| `uv run strata artifact <cmd> [--artifact-dir DIR]` | Inspect the server's configured artifact store (its metadata DSN and blob backend included) without a running server, or one local SQLite store with `--artifact-dir`: `list`, `show <ref>`, `lineage <ref>` (renders model ← features ← scan ← table @ snapshot), `pull <ref> --to FILE`, `audit [name]` (registry history), `pending` (approval queue), `verify`, `gc` (collect what nothing holds, least recently used first; `--dry-run` to preview, `--max-bytes`, `--max-idle-days`, `--min-idle-seconds`). Also publishes and moves results: `publish` / `unpublish` (a link anyone can open), `promote` (copy an artifact and its chain to the team store and name it there), `export` (write a tabular artifact into an Iceberg table), `archive` (a self-contained bundle: page, bytes, manifest, README). `<ref>` is a name, `id@v=N`, or bare id. |
| `uv run strata migrate --to-dsn <dsn>` | Copy artifact-store metadata from SQLite to Postgres. Setting `STRATA_ARTIFACT_METADATA_DSN` alone starts an empty store; this carries an existing one across. Metadata only: blobs are configured separately. |
| `uv run strata apikey <cmd>` | Mint, list and revoke API keys for a server running with `auth_mode="api_key"`: `create`, `list` (never shows secrets), `revoke <id>`. |
| `uv run strata env gc` | Remove shared environments no notebook links to. Only relevant with the shared environment backend. See [Environments](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/environment/). |
| `uv run strata watch [dir\|--session]` | Attach the read-only terminal viewer to a live notebook session without writing any config (unlike `strata agent`). Needs the `[tui]` extra. See [Terminal viewer](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/tui/). |
| `uv run strata-notebook-tui` | Read-only terminal viewer that attaches to a running notebook session. Needs the `[tui]` extra. See [Terminal viewer](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/tui/). |
| `strata-worker --port 9000` | Start a remote worker for `# @worker` cells. It binds `127.0.0.1` unless `STRATA_WORKER_TOKEN` is set (then `0.0.0.0`) or `--host` says otherwise. Run the installed binary (for example `.venv/bin/strata-worker`), not through `uv run`, whose process would keep `STRATA_WORKER_TOKEN` readable to cells. With `--connect wss://...` it binds no port and dials out to a relay instead. See [Workers](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/workers/). |

In a checkout with the venv activated (`source .venv/bin/activate`),
you can drop the prefix too.

## Development commands

```bash
# Sync with all optional extras - matches CI. Required for the test
# suite because the harness fixtures point the per-notebook venv at
# the dev interpreter, so the dev env needs the [notebook] extra
# (orjson, pyarrow, cloudpickle) for cell-execution tests.
uv sync --all-extras

# Run all tests
uv run pytest

# Format and lint
uv run pre-commit run --all-files

# Type check (scope is set in pyproject.toml, as in CI)
uv run ty check

# Start frontend dev server (hot reload, proxies to backend)
cd frontend && npm run dev
```

### Integration test dependencies

The end-to-end integration script needs a real PostgreSQL instance for
its Iceberg SQL catalog. A throwaway Postgres container is shipped
as `docker-compose.test.yml`:

```bash
# Start the test Postgres (port 5432)
docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d

# Run the integration script against it (starts its own server)
STRATA_CATALOG_URI=postgresql://strata:strata@localhost:5432/iceberg_catalog \
  uv run python scripts/integration_test.py --start-server

# Tear it down
docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml down
```

The compose file is dev-only: it has no health-bound dependency on
the main `docker-compose.yml`, and the credentials are intentionally
fixed (`strata`/`strata`) for predictable local connection strings.

<!-- https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/notebook/index.md -->

# Your first notebook

Strata Notebook is an interactive notebook with content-addressed
caching, automatic dependency tracking, and cascade execution. This
quickstart walks through a real three-cell pipeline, then surfaces
the distinctive features (prompt cells, cascade, cache hits) on top
of it.

This is the **web UI** quickstart - you drive the notebook in a
browser. The same notebook can also be driven by a
[coding agent](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/agent/) or watched live from a
[terminal](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/tui/).

![The Strata notebook UI: two named Python cells, load and summarize, each with
its source and an interactive table of results, the Notebook settings rail
collapsed on the right, and a bottom drawer showing the DAG of load, summarize
and plot with per-cell timings.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/notebook-anatomy-light.png#only-light)
![The Strata notebook UI: two named Python cells, load and summarize, each with
its source and an interactive table of results, the Notebook settings rail
collapsed on the right, and a bottom drawer showing the DAG of load, summarize
and plot with per-cell timings.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/notebook-anatomy-dark.png#only-dark)

The pipeline below is the one in that screenshot.

## 1. Take the tutorial

Strata ships sample notebooks that run without an API key, so there is nothing to clone.
Start with the two-minute one on what the cache saves.

=== "uv (recommended)"

    Install the CLI from PyPI into a uv-managed tool environment, then
    open the tutorial:

    ```bash
    uv tool install "strata-notebook[mcp,tui]"
    strata tutorial caching
    ```

    Open the URL it prints. Requires [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/);
    plain `pip install` is not supported.

    The `mcp` and `tui` extras are for `strata agent` and `strata watch`
    (see [What's next](#whats-next)); the web UI needs neither. SQL
    cells need the `sql` extra plus a driver extra for each database,
    for example
    `uv tool install "strata-notebook[mcp,tui,sql,sql-duckdb,sql-sqlite]"`;
    without it a notebook that holds a SQL cell does not open.

=== "Docker"

    ```bash
    docker compose up -d --build
    ```

    The compose file runs Strata in personal mode (single-user,
    writes enabled). See [Docker deployment](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/deployment/docker/)
    for details.

    Open [http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765) and pick
    **Open a sample** on the home page.

=== "From source (one-time setup)"

    Clone the repo, then install it and build the frontend:

    ```bash
    uv sync                      # Python deps + Strata, editable
    cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build && cd ..
    ```

    Then open the tutorial:

    ```bash
    uv run strata tutorial caching
    ```

    Open the URL it prints. The npm step above is one-time setup,
    not part of the recurring start command.

`strata tutorial caching` copies the sample into your storage directory under a fresh
name, so you can edit it freely. It uses the server on `:8765`, or starts one if none is
running and keeps it until you press ++ctrl+c++ (pass `--server` for another address).
The first open builds the copy's environment before it returns, so it takes a little
longer. `strata tutorial` alone lists the samples.

The rest of this page builds a pipeline of your own. Leave that server running. On later
sessions, start one with `strata-notebook` (`uv run strata-notebook` from source). Personal
mode is the default (single-user, writes enabled), so a local run needs no configuration.

## 2. Create a notebook

Click **New Notebook** on the home page at
[http://localhost:8765](http://localhost:8765). Pick a name, a parent
directory under the notebook storage root, and a Python version.
Strata creates a directory containing `notebook.toml`, a per-notebook
`pyproject.toml`, and a `cells/` folder.

The notebook opens empty - click **+ Add cell** and pick a kind to
write the first one.

By default the storage root is `~/.strata/notebooks` - **not** the
directory you launched from - so new notebooks land there regardless of
your shell's working directory. To put them somewhere else (the current
directory is a common choice), start the server with `--notebook-dir`:

```bash
strata-notebook --notebook-dir .          # current directory
strata-notebook --notebook-dir ~/work/nb  # or any path
```

(or set `STRATA_NOTEBOOK_STORAGE_DIR`). The server prints the active
location on startup.

Each notebook gets its own Python environment, managed by `uv`, so
installing pandas in one notebook doesn't touch another. Everything
autosaves: source goes to `cells/`, runtime state to `.strata/`.
Both diff cleanly in git, no JSON blobs in commits.

### Cell types

The **+ Add cell** menu offers six kinds, and Python is the default.
A cell's kind is fixed when you create it - the kind shown in the cell
header is a label, not a picker - so to change one, delete the cell and
re-add it with the kind you want.

| Kind | What it's for |
| --- | --- |
| **Python** | Regular Python code. Most cells. |
| **SQL** | A SQL query against a declared connection. Connection name is an annotation; the result is a pyarrow Table available downstream. Needs the `sql` extra and a driver extra (see [Install](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/getting-started/installation/)). |
| **R** | R code - stats and tidyverse. See [Cell kinds](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/guides/cells/). |
| **Prompt** | LLM call as a DAG node. The body is a template with `{{ variable }}` substitution from upstream cells; the response is cached as an artifact like any other cell output. |
| **Widget** | A declarative control panel - one control per line (`alpha = slider(0, 1)`, plus number/dropdown/checkbox/text). Each control is an input downstream cells consume; with **⚡ Live** on, dragging one recomputes the cells that depend on it. |
| **Markdown** | Prose between cells. Rendered as HTML; not part of the DAG. |

Two more shapes are **annotations on a Python cell** rather than menu
entries - you add a Python cell and put the annotation on its first
line:

| Shape | Annotation |
| --- | --- |
| **Loop** | `# @loop max_iter=N carry=state` - re-runs the cell with `carry` threaded across iterations, one artifact per step. |
| **Variant** | `# @variant group name` - several cells share one DAG slot, for A/B-ing implementations of the same step. |

Library, mount, and worker shapes are annotation-driven too. See
[Cell kinds](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/guides/cells/) for the full surface and
[Annotations](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/reference/annotations/) for every annotation.

## 3. Walk through a pipeline

Three cells, one real DAG. We'll load the iris dataset, summarize
by species, and plot a scatter.

**Before typing**, open **Notebook settings** in the sidebar, then the
**Environment** panel, and add `scikit-learn`, `pandas`, and `matplotlib`. Each `uv add` runs
in the background and the notebook surfaces a sync banner while it's
working. Wait for the banner to clear before running the first cell.

!!! note "Display rendering"
    The output blocks below are shown as text for the doc. In the
    UI, DataFrames render in an interactive grid (page, sort, filter,
    and search over the full cached artifact, with CSV / Parquet
    export), matplotlib figures render as inline PNGs, prompt-cell
    responses render as structured JSON (when `@output_schema` is set)
    or markdown.

### Load the data

```python
# @name load
import time
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris

time.sleep(2)  # simulate the latency of a real fetch
iris = load_iris(as_frame=True)
df = iris.frame.copy()
df["species"] = pd.Categorical.from_codes(df["target"], iris.target_names)
feature_names = iris.feature_names
df.head()
```

```text title="Output"
   sepal length (cm)  sepal width (cm)  petal length (cm)  petal width (cm)  target species
0                5.1               3.5                1.4               0.2       0  setosa
1                4.9               3.0                1.4               0.2       0  setosa
2                4.7               3.2                1.3               0.2       0  setosa
3                4.6               3.1                1.5               0.2       0  setosa
4                5.0               3.6                1.4               0.2       0  setosa
```

The `# @name load` line labels the cell in the DAG view and its header; without
it, a cell is labelled by the variables it defines. See
[`@name`](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/reference/annotations/python/#name).

Press ++shift+enter++. The first run pauses ~2 seconds (the simulated
fetch) and the DataFrame preview renders below the cell.

### Summarize by species

```python
# @name summarize
stats = df.groupby("species", observed=True)[feature_names].mean().round(2)
stats
```

```text title="Output"
            sepal length (cm)  sepal width (cm)  petal length (cm)  petal width (cm)
species
setosa                   5.01              3.43               1.46              0.25
versicolor               5.94              2.77               4.26              1.33
virginica                6.59              2.97               5.55              2.03
```

Strata reads this cell's AST, sees it references `df` and `feature_names`
from the loader, and wires an edge. The DAG view in the bottom
drawer (click **expand**) shows the dependency.

### Plot

```python
# @name plot
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 4))
for species, group in df.groupby("species", observed=True):
    ax.scatter(
        group["sepal length (cm)"],
        group["petal length (cm)"],
        label=str(species),
        alpha=0.7,
    )
ax.set_xlabel("Sepal length (cm)")
ax.set_ylabel("Petal length (cm)")
ax.legend()
fig
```

The matplotlib figure renders inline as a PNG.

## 4. Re-run for cache hits

Press ++shift+enter++ on the loader cell again. The 2-second pause
is gone, Strata returned the cached `df` instantly, and the cell
header shows a **cached** badge with what it saved. The right of the
header gives the load time ("loaded in 5ms" or similar).

The cache is content-addressed: the cache key is a hash of the
cell's source, its upstream artifacts, and the environment lockfile.
Re-running with the same three is a cache hit. No `@memoize`,
no manual invalidation, and the cached result is byte-identical to
what produced it the first time. The notebook keeps each cell's
current value plus its last 3 earlier ones
([`STRATA_NOTEBOOK_KEEP_SUPERSEDED_VERSIONS`](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/reference/configuration/#notebook)),
so reverting a recent edit is a hit too and an older value is
computed again. A cell's console output is keyed by the same hash and
replayed with it, so even a cell that only `print`s and feeds nothing
downstream is cached. A cell that must always
run (a side effect, a live API call, a fresh random draw) opts out
with [`# @nocache`](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/reference/annotations/python/#nocache).

## 5. Edit upstream, watch the cascade

Edit the loader, say, change `time.sleep(2)` to `time.sleep(1)`.
Strata re-analyzes the source and computes a new provenance hash, so
the loader's cached result no longer matches its source and the cell
flips **stale**. So do the summary and plot cells: they referenced
`df`, which is no longer the cached value. (Hover **Why stale?** on
any of them to see the reason: `source changed` on the loader,
`upstream changed` on the others.)

Now press ++shift+enter++ on the plot cell. Strata walks back through
the stale upstream cells and runs loader → summary → plot in
topological order, with a live progress strip showing which cell is
executing. There is no confirmation step: cascades run automatically,
so running a cell always gives you a result computed from current
inputs.

![The same notebook after the loader is edited: the loader reads stale, with a
"Why stale?" pill and its old output dimmed under "Output from the previous
run", and all three cells are outlined in amber in the DAG below.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/cascade-stale-light.png#only-light)
![The same notebook after the loader is edited: the loader reads stale, with a
"Why stale?" pill and its old output dimmed under "Output from the previous
run", and all three cells are outlined in amber in the DAG below.](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/assets/cascade-stale-dark.png#only-dark)

Revert the edit (`time.sleep(1)` back to `time.sleep(2)`) and
re-run: every cell becomes a cache hit on the way through, no work
happens, the cascade short-circuits to milliseconds.

## 6. Add a prompt cell (optional)

Prompt cells are the most distinctive Strata feature beyond caching.
The body is a template; the response is a cached DAG node like any
other cell.

In the cell menu, click **+ Add cell** and pick **Prompt**. Paste
this in:

```text
# @model claude-sonnet-4-6
# @temperature 0.3
# @system You are a botanist describing distinguishing features of iris species.

Given these per-species feature means, write one sentence per
species describing its most distinguishing trait:

{{ stats }}
```

Hit ++shift+enter++. The `{{ stats }}` placeholder gets substituted
with the upstream DataFrame, the prompt goes to the configured LLM,
and the response is stored as an artifact keyed by `(template,
inputs, model config)`. Running again with the same upstream
`stats` and the same template is a cache hit, no second API call.

Needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (or another provider's key) configured in
the Runtime panel. See [Provider configuration](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/guides/cells/prompt/#provider-configuration)
for provider setup and [Prompt cells](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/guides/cells/prompt/#prompt-cells)
for the full annotation surface (`@output_schema`, `@validate_retries`).

## 7. Other display types

The cells above used trailing expressions for the DataFrame and
the matplotlib `Figure`. Other shapes you can put at the end of a
cell, or call from `display()`:

| Trailing expression | Renders as |
| --- | --- |
| pandas DataFrame / Series | Interactive grid: page, sort, filter, and search over the full cached artifact, with CSV / Parquet export. |
| matplotlib `Figure` | Inline PNG. |
| PIL `Image` | Inline PNG. |
| dict / list / primitive | Fenced JSON block. |
| numpy ndarray | A one-line summary of its shape and dtype. |
| `Markdown("**hi**")` | The `Markdown` helper renders inline HTML. |
| `Image.open(...)` | Rendered inline as PNG. Video and audio are not display types; store them as artifacts and open them outside the notebook. |

Use `display(x)` for **multiple** outputs in one cell (each call
adds a new render below the cell). For one trailing expression at
the end, no `display()` needed: the harness auto-displays it.

## Cell operations

| Action | How |
| --- | --- |
| Run cell | ++shift+enter++ or **Run** button in gutter |
| Add cell | **Add cell below** button in gutter, or **Add cell** in the header |
| Delete cell | **Delete cell** button in gutter |
| Duplicate cell | **Duplicate cell** button in gutter |
| Move cell | **Move up** / **Move down** buttons in gutter |
| Change cell kind | Not editable - delete and re-add with the new kind |
| Keyboard help | Press ++question++ |

## What's next

- [Use a coding agent](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/agent/): hand this notebook to Claude Code and watch it build, in a browser or a terminal - one command sets it up
- [Agent scratchpad](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/scratchpad/): the other way round - an agent working on something else using a notebook as **cached** throwaway compute instead of temp scripts; installs as a one-command plugin
- [Terminal viewer](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/tui/) to watch this notebook live from a terminal with `strata watch ./my-notebook`
- [Concepts](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/concepts/caching/) for how the DAG, caching, and cascade work
- [Cell kinds](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/guides/cells/) for the full surface (Python, prompt, SQL, R, widget, markdown, loop, variant)
- [Annotations](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/reference/annotations/) for `@worker`, `@mount`, `@loop`, and friends
- [Workers](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/workers/) for `# @worker gpu-fly` and dispatching to remote compute
- [Coming from Jupyter](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/import/) for `strata import nb.ipynb`
- [Export and import](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/export/) for sharing a notebook as a single self-contained markdown or HTML file, or as a snapshot bundle (state and artifacts) that imports back
- [Environment](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/environment/) for package management and Python versions
- [How Strata compares](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/comparison/)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](https://bearingresearch.com/strata/dev/notebook/keyboard/)
